messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: elevated 5xx rate for sapling-prod-us-west-2 on Dedicated - triggered at 2026-03-15T21:04:27Z. Symptom: high 5xx (mostly 502/504) + p95 latency spike. Auto-run diagnostics: kv-eviction-rate=high, inflight_queue_depth=~820, avg_seq_len=1400, nodes_reporting=6

maya-oncall: acked. I'm on it. sapling-facing svc is sapling-infer-prod on pool:dedicated-usw2-a. Eden, can you confirm impact on your end?

eden-customer-sre: seeing ~12% 5xx and timeouts for batch endpoints since ~21:02. Lots of retries from our side. Impacting conversion pipeline.

maya-oncall: thanks. quick check: `kubectl -n dedicated get pods -l tenant=sapling -o wide` shows a couple pods at 3/4 restarts. Pulling logs now.

luis-eng: chiming in — telemetry shows one tenant (sparkline-analytics) doing sustained long-sequence streaming + large batch submits (batch_size=128, seq_len median 1200) on same pool. KV cache evictions correlate with their client_id. Could be noisy neighbor.

maya-oncall: copying logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T21:03:45Z ERROR inference: upstream read timeout (read ECONNRESET) model=redwood-open-7b tenant=sapling request_id=xyz
2026-03-15T21:03:46Z WARN kvcache: eviction rate spike tenant=sparkline-analytics evicted=1420
```


dave-sre: joining handoff. If sparkline workload is thrashing KV, that would cause higher cold-starts and longer tails -> gateway timeouts. We should try immediate mitigations: 1) isolate sparkline to a different pool or cordon node(s), 2) throttle them via per-tenant inflight limit, 3) route sapling traffic to standby nodes. Which is fastest?

kiran-support: node cordon + cordon drain will take a few mins and may evict more. Quickest low-risk is to flip per-tenant circuit breaker for sparkline to max_inflight=30 and reduce their batch_size via API gateway. I can push a throttle policy now.

maya-oncall: do it. Kiran, can you also route sapling to fallback pool `dedicated-usw2-b-standby`? It's warmed but not fully serving — will accept traffic with slightly higher latency but far fewer 5xxs.

kiran-support: applying throttle policy -> `rbacctl apply tenant-throttle sparkline-analytics --max-inflight=30 --priority=low` -> response: queued. Pushing route for sapling -> `routingctl set-target sapling-infer-prod dedicated-usw2-b-standby` -> ok, push accepted.

luis-eng: monitoring: sapling 5xx dropping to ~3% after route switch. p95 latency for sapling up from 1.2s -> 1.6s but stable. Sparkline still causing KV evictions on the original pool.

dave-sre: okay we need a short-term capacity increase to avoid recurrence. Plan: scale dedicated-usw2-a by +2 nodes and cordon the worst offending pods for the noisy tenant. Maya, can you coordinate with infra-autoscale?

maya-oncall: pinging ops-runbook-bot to run scale.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook trigger accepted: scale_group=dedicated-usw2-a, delta=+2 nodes. Estimated spin up 4-6m. Change owner: maya-oncall.

emails@example.com: (system) Notifying oncall and customer SREs of mitigation action.

eden-customer-sre: appreciated. Are we expecting any data loss or dropped in-flight requests for sapling?

maya-oncall: no data loss expected. We routed new traffic to standby; in-flight on old pool will complete or be retried by client. Recommend sapling reduce client-retry-window for 1hr while we stabilize.

kiran-support: sparkline throttle applied. Observed their tail-latency drop ~70% and evictions down. Starting selective eviction of heavy jobs: `jobctl cancel --tenant sparkline-analytics --label=heavy-batch --grace=30s` -> cancelled 8 jobs.

luis-eng: after cancelling heavy jobs, KV eviction rate down to normal. Node CPU/mem pressure dropping. Dedicated-usw2-a reporting healthy again.

dave-sre: good. Actions summary being posted to incident channel and we'll do an oncall handoff at shift change. Immediate next steps: 1) follow up with sparkline account team to enforce quotas (account action), 2) add per-tenant max_batch config to default policy, 3) increase capacity headroom for popular pools, 4) postmortem.

maya-oncall: I'm going to mark this as mitigated for sapling. Reopen if 5xx >5% again. Logging the incident id: INC-2026-0315-3751234567. Handoff to dave-sre for follow-ups.

dave-sre: taking follow-ups. I'll coordinate with customer success for the sapling impact email. Also creating a JIRA: RED-INC-2318 for quota + runbook updates.

e den-customer-sre: thanks all — please share ETA for permanent mitigation. We'll expect a follow-up email.

kiran-support: note for postmortem: add metric alert for per-tenant kv-eviction-rate and inflight queue ratio.

maya-oncall: closing slack loop here. :thumbsup: If anyone sees a regression, ping #oncall immediately and I will re-open.

(automated) incident-bot: incident status -> MITIGATED. duration ~16m. root cause: noisy neighbor (sparkline large-batch long-seq workload) causing KV evictions and inflight queue saturation leading to gateway 5xx for sapling. Next steps assigned in JIRA RED-INC-2318.
